correctness.rationale: Reran committed verifier in inputs/artifacts: V1 counts {0:1,1:1,2:2,3:5,4:16,5:63,6:318} OK; V2 poset axioms OK (406 types); V3 pairwise non-isomorphism by independent set-based S_n signature OK; V4 coefficient/value consistency, Lvals[1]=#ideals, lead*n! == e, h* agreement and sum==e OK (406 types); V5 independent backtracking linear-extension replay OK; V6 Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity L(-m)=(-1)^n S(m-1) OK (406 types, m=1..n+1); V7 maximality replay OK; ALL VERIFY_OK. Auditor independently brute-forced weak order-preserving maps by enumerating all functions on random types (n=2..6, m<=3): all matched stored Lvals. Auditor independently brute-forced strict maps (n=3..5, k=1..3) and confirmed reciprocity identity against stored coefficients. Auditor independently counted linear extensions by permutation scan on random n=4,5 types: matched stored e. Closed forms confirmed: antichain n=6 Lvals=(m+1)^6 values 1,64,729,4096,15625,46656,117649, h*=(1,57,302,302,57,1,0), e=720; chain n=6 Lvals=C(m+6,6) values 1,7,28,84,210,462,924, h*=(1,0,0,0,0,0,0), e=1. n=6 sorted e top5 = 720,360,240,240,180, min 1; maxima per n 1,1,2,6,24,120,720 each uniquely at idx 0 (antichain). n=0 boundary handled (single type, Lvals [1], coef [1], h* [1]). Completeness rests on the standard lemma that every iso class meets the naturally-labelled (upper-triangular transitive) set via a linear extension, quotiented by full-relation S_n-minimum canonical key; the independent set-based canonical path in verify.py agrees. The label '# unimodular top simplices of the Stanley triangulation' is explicitly presented as the meaning of the second linear-extension count via cited Stanley theory, not as an independent geometric triangulation computation; DRAFT states what is proved by computation vs cited. Result is therefore machine-established computation with exact integer/Fraction arithmetic and independent replay, not hand proof — as claimed.

originality.rationale: Volume values alone are mechanically implied: FindStat St000100 publishes exact e(P) for every poset type to n=7+, and Stanley Vol(O(P))=e(P)/n! converts them to normalized volumes. The headline, however, is the full per-type Ehrhart polynomial + h* + values with dual agreement, exhaustive maximality replay, and per-type reciprocity over all 406 types n<=6. That artifact is not implied: at n=6 there are 62 distinct e values but 121 distinct Ehrhart Lvals vectors, and same-e types exist with distinct Ehrhart polynomials (e.g. e=4 class with 9 types in 2 Ehrhart classes). No triaged source publishes it. Live checks: OEIS A000112 gives only universe counts; FindStat Posets collection gives the (E,n) canonical universe to n=7 and its 85-statistic list has no full-Ehrhart-coefficient statistic (closest: St000100 linear extensions, St000104/St000151 polytope facets, St000524 # sharing an order polynomial, St000635 strict endomorphisms into itself); arXiv 'order polytope AND Ehrhart' (38 hits) sampled entries are family-specific (zig-zag/crown/snake/skew/Gelfand-Tsetlin, enriched/marked/q-analogues, flow equivalences) or general theorems (Liu-Xin-Zhang dim<=13 Ehrhart positivity/real-rootedness; Liu-Tsuchiya d>=21 non-positivity; Ferroni-Morales-Panova skew positivity; Chappell-Friedl-Sanyal double posets) — none is an exhaustive 318-type n=6 Ehrhart table. Foundational Stanley (1986) gives general formulas, Brinkmann-McKay gives enumeration only. Internal prior SCOPE061 (linear-extension census to n=8) implies volumes but not Ehrhart polynomials, triangulation agreement, or reciprocity. Certification/replay treated as evidence only; novelty is the per-type Ehrhart census itself.

value.rationale: The strongest headline — the complete exact Ehrhart-polynomial/h*/volume table for every unlabeled order polytope with n<=6 — is an exact invariant of a specific natural object (order polytopes of the OEIS/FindStat-backed universe: 1,1,2,5,16,63,318 types) motivated before computation by the recognized Stanley order-polytope program (volume = linear extensions, Ehrhart = order-preserving maps, canonical triangulation, reciprocity) feeding Ehrhart-positivity, chain-polytope, and reflexive programs. The values are not known or mechanically implied (full polynomials strictly refine e(P)/volumes: 121 vs 62 distinct values at n=6). A future researcher can reasonably need the precise fact for a given poset type (order polynomial, h*, volume) or as an exact anchor/benchmark for lattice-point and triangulation software; per-type dual volume agreement and reciprocity make each entry checkable. This is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration: scope n<=6 is the first width/dimension/volume-diverse window, and every entry carries dual cross-checks. The per-n maxima (n! uniquely at the antichain) are mathematically trivial in isolation but are honestly presented as the certified extremal anchor of the census, not the sole contribution, and do not diminish the table's independent retrievability.

decisive_checks: Reran committed verify.py from stored tables: ALL VERIFY_OK (V1 counts, V2 axioms, V3 non-isomorphism, V4 coeff/value/h*/volume equality, V5 lin-ext replay, V6 reciprocity, V7 maximality).
Independent brute-force weak-map enumeration (all functions) on random types n=2..6 matched stored Lvals; independent brute-force strict-map enumeration matched reciprocity identity.
Independent permutation-scan linear-extension counts on random n=4,5 types matched stored e; antichain (m+1)^n and chain C(m+n,n) closed forms confirmed including n=6 examples and h* vectors.
Distinctness analysis: n=6 has 121 distinct Ehrhart Lvals vs 62 distinct e values; same-e/different-Ehrhart classes exist — full table not implied by FindStat e(P).
Maxima replay: per-n maxima 1,1,2,6,24,120,720 each uniquely at idx 0; n=6 top5 720,360,240,240,180, min 1.

residual_risks: Completeness of the 406-type universe relies on the standard (but code-assumed) lemma that every isomorphism class contains a naturally labelled representative via a linear extension; external OEIS/FindStat counts agree but are consistency only.

Identification of the second linear-extension count with the number of top simplices of the Stanley triangulation relies on cited Stanley theory, explicitly flagged as background rather than recomputed geometry.

Correctness is machine-certified (exact integer/Fraction stdlib computation plus independent replay), not a hand proof; a shared systematic misinterpretation of the order-polytope/lattice-point correspondence would survive replay, mitigated by brute-force function-enumeration spot checks.

Originality search sampled arXiv API abstracts and the FindStat statistic list rather than full text of every paper; a buried full 318-type table in an unrelated venue cannot be logically excluded but no such source surfaced.
